title: Wall-to-Wall Carpet vs Area Rug Over Hardwood: Which Makes Sense?
meta: Wall-to-wall carpet or an area rug over hardwood? For Sammamish homes: carpet wins bedrooms, stairs and bonus rooms, rugs win the main floor. Wills Flooring.
keywords: wall to wall carpet vs area rug, area rug over hardwood floors, carpet or rug over hardwood, should I carpet over hardwood, carpet vs rug bedroom Sammamish

blocks.lead: Wall-to-wall carpet makes sense in bedrooms, bonus rooms and on stairs, where you want warmth and quiet all the way to the wall. An area rug makes sense wherever the hardwood is worth showing, which in most Sammamish homes means the whole main floor.
blocks.detail: The wrong answer is carpeting over good main-floor hardwood, or asking a rug to do the job of carpet in a cold upstairs bedroom. Carpet labor is $0.99 per sq ft and $30 per step, so the upstairs decision is usually cheaper than people assume once you compare it with a room-size rug.

blocks.html: This question comes up in almost every Sammamish estimate. The plateau homes in Klahanie, Trossachs and Pine Lake were built between the 1990s and 2010s with builder-grade oak on the main floor and carpet upstairs. Twenty years later the carpet is tired and the oak is scratched, and the owner asks: do I put carpet back, refinish the oak and use rugs, or carpet over the wood and stop thinking about it? Here is how we answer, room by room.

blocks.text: What you are really choosing between

items.title: Warmth and quiet
items.text: Wall-to-wall carpet with a good pad insulates the whole room and kills footfall noise between floors. A rug does that only inside its own footprint. In a two-story home with kids upstairs, that is the whole argument for carpeting the bedrooms.

items.title: Look and resale
items.text: Eastside buyers expect to see hardwood on the main floor. A rug frames the wood and changes with the furniture. Carpet over good hardwood reads as hiding something, and an agent will say so at the listing walk-through.

items.title: Cleaning reality
items.text: A rug can be rolled up, sent out for cleaning or replaced after a bad spill. Carpet is cleaned in place, and the pad holds whatever soaks through. With dogs, that matters more than any fiber label.

items.title: Flexibility
items.text: A rug is furniture: move, sell or swap it any time. Carpet is a 10 to 15 year commitment, and over hardwood it means tack strips nailed into the wood along every wall.

blocks.note: This pattern holds across Sahalee, Beaver Lake and Klahanie. Your layout may argue for an exception, which is what the visit is for.

blocks.text: What rugs quietly do to hardwood

items.html: Fade lines. South-facing plateau rooms get real sun. The wood under a rug ends up a different shade than the exposed floor, and the line only disappears with a full sand.
Pad discoloration. Cheap rubber or latex rug pads react with the finish and leave a cloudy patch the exact shape of the pad. Use a felt pad rated for hardwood.
Trapped grit. Driveway sand works under the rug edge and scratches the finish as the rug shifts. Vacuum under it, not just on top.
Moisture. A dog bowl or a plant on a rug over hardwood is a slow leak you cannot see. Black stains mean water reached the boards weeks ago.

blocks.text: Price the carpet side in Sammamish

blocks.html: Rugs are furniture and priced like furniture. Carpet has a published labor rate, so you can compare honestly. Stretch-in over pad is $0.99 per sq ft, stairs are $30 per step, tear-out and haul-away is $0.45 per sq ft, moving furniture is $0.25, and there is a 500 sq ft minimum. A Klahanie upstairs, four bedrooms and a hall at 1,100 sq ft plus a 15-step run, is 1,100 × $0.99 + 15 × $30 = $1,539 in labor. One bedroom alone still bills at the minimum, $495, which is why people do the floor as one job. Carpet and pad come on top, quoted at the free estimate.

blocks.note: Stretch-in is the only method we use over hardwood. Glue-down is for slabs, never over wood you might want to refinish.

blocks.text: When wall-to-wall is wrong, and when a rug is wrong

a.title: The floor under it is an asset
items: There is sound hardwood underneath, especially on the main floor
Someone has dust or pet allergies and the room is shared living space
The room takes water: kitchens, entries, laundry, bathrooms
You plan to sell soon and the oak just needs a refinish

b.title: You are asking it to be carpet
items: The room is an upstairs bedroom that is cold and echoes
You need the whole floor quiet for someone sleeping below
The surface is stairs: loose rugs and runners on stairs are a fall hazard
You would need a rug covering 90 percent of the floor anyway

blocks.title: The one thing we talk people out of:
blocks.text: Carpeting over main-floor hardwood because it is scratched. Refinishing at $3.99 per sq ft removes the scratches and keeps the value. Carpet over it adds tack-strip holes and a job to undo when you sell. If the wood is thick enough to sand, sand it.
Mistakes Sammamish homeowners make with this decision

items.title: Buying the rug before the dog
items.text: A light wool rug on a main floor with a lab that swims in Pine Lake will be brown by fall. With a dog, choose a patterned, mid-tone rug or a solution-dyed carpet.

items.title: Rugs that are too small
items.text: A rug floating in the middle of an open-plan great room looks like a bath mat. The front legs of every seat should sit on it. Measure the furniture group first, then shop.

items.title: Gluing carpet to hardwood
items.text: Glue-down carpet over oak is the worst of both worlds. The adhesive soaks into the grain and the floor is never refinishable again. If carpet must go over wood, it is stretch-in over pad, nothing else.

items.title: Carpeting the whole upstairs the same
items.text: Bedrooms want a soft, dense pile. A bonus room with a pool table wants a low, tight loop that takes abuse. Two carpets upstairs is normal and the labor rate does not change.

items: Lift a rug corner or a closet carpet edge to see what wood is under the main floor
List every room and mark it warm-and-quiet (carpet) or show-the-wood (rug)
Check which rooms get afternoon sun; those need carpet or a rug you can rotate
Decide whether the stairs stay hardwood; if kids or an older dog use them daily, plan carpet at $30 per step
Ask how tack strips will be handled over hardwood, and confirm no glue
Bring the fiber question to the estimate; the fiber comparison covers what holds up with dogs and kids
Get the whole plan on one written quote so carpet and refinishing are priced together

faq.q: Can you install wall-to-wall carpet over hardwood floors without damaging them?
faq.a: Yes, if it is stretch-in carpet over pad, which is the $0.99 per sq ft method. Tack strips are nailed along the walls and leave small perimeter holes that sand out later. Never glue carpet to hardwood; the adhesive ruins the wood for refinishing.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to put a rug on hardwood or install carpet?
faq.a: For one room they are closer than people think. Carpet labor carries a 500 sq ft minimum, so a single bedroom bills at 500 × $0.99 = $495 plus carpet and pad, while a good room-size wool rug can cost as much on its own. Carpet pulls ahead once you do the whole upstairs at once.

faq.q: Does carpet over hardwood hurt resale value in Sammamish?
faq.a: On the main floor, yes. Eastside buyers expect visible hardwood in living and dining areas and mentally deduct the cost of removing carpet. In upstairs bedrooms it is neutral or positive, since most buyers here still prefer carpet where they sleep.

faq.q: What kind of rug pad is safe on hardwood?
faq.a: Felt, or felt with a natural rubber underside, made for hardwood. Avoid cheap PVC or synthetic rubber waffle pads, which react with the finish and leave a cloudy patch. Trim the pad an inch inside the rug edge so it lies flat.

faq.q: Should the stairs be carpeted if the main floor is hardwood?
faq.a: Often, yes. Hardwood stairs are slippery in socks and hard on older dogs. Carpet at $30 per step, or a properly stapled runner, gives grip and quiet while still showing wood at the edges. Loose runners on stairs are a fall hazard.

faq.q: Will a rug leave a mark on my hardwood floor?
faq.a: It can. Sunlight changes the color of the finish and the wood, so the covered area ends up a different shade. Rotate rugs twice a year and shift them a few inches. Only a full sand and refinish erases a fade line.
